bugs.description: The `// Previously this used a fixed window; changed to a token bucket after the review pointed out the burst behavior.` comment narrates the edit history and the review that produced the code. A comment describes the code as it exists now.
bugs.detection_hint: previously this used|process narration|edit narration|historical narration|narrates the (?:edit|change|history)

bugs.description: The `// Per the reviewer's request, the burst multiplier stays configurable.` comment refers to the review conversation that produced the code. It carries no meaning outside the run that wrote it.
bugs.detection_hint: per the reviewer|conversation reference|references the review|reviewer's request

bugs.description: The `// Refills the bucket every 30 seconds.` comment contradicts the code: REFILL_INTERVAL_MS is 15_000. A misleading comment is worse than no comment; the change updates or deletes it.
bugs.detection_hint: every 30 seconds|stale comment|obsolete comment|comment[^.]{0,60}(?:contradict|no longer|out of date)|15_?000

bugs.description: The `// handle edge case` comment names no condition, risk, or dependency. Precise language names the exact case — here, a cost above the bucket's capacity.
The `// Mirrors the guard in the function two above.` comment refers to a file position that any reordering breaks. A comment names symbols, never positions.

non_violations.description: The sweep() comment documents an ordering guarantee and the consequence of violating it — the permitted why-comment class, not a violation.
The bucketKeyForUser comment says 'user' in the domain sense (an end user of the product). The conversation-reference rule keys to the run that produced the code, never to vocabulary.

The acquireToken doc comment documents a public contract's failure mode and the caller's obligation. The comment ban covers in-body comments that restate the code; this doc comment adds contract information the signature does not carry, so it satisfies the rule.
